\begin{theorem}[Third-order invariance estimate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_c3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_c3}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.independent_polynomial_coupling, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_c3_of_independent_pair, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive.identDistrib, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.influence}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability spaces, and let
$F$ be a multilinear coefficient family on subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ of degree at
most $k$. Suppose $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent under $\mu$ and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ are
independent under $\nu$, and that each coordinate variable is
$(2,3,\rho)$-hypercontractive for some $0<\rho<1$, has mean zero, and has second moment
one. If $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is three times continuously differentiable and
$|\psi'''(t)|\le C$ for all $t$, where $C\ge0$, then
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\mu\psi(F(X))-\mathbb E_\nu\psi(F(Y))\right|
\le \frac{C}{3}\left(\frac1\rho\right)^{3k}\sum_{i=1}^n \mathrm{Inf}_i[F]^{{3}/{2}}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Invariance under small noisy influences]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_no_notables}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_no_notables}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.highDegree_noise_l2Norm_le_exp, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_cutoff_exp, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_cutoff_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_cutoff_power_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_lowDegree_tail, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_noiseOp_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, KKL.highDegreePart, KKL.influence_lowDegreePart_le, KKL.influence_noiseOp_le_noisyInfluence, KKL.lowDegreePart, KKL.noisyInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
There is a constant $K>0$ such that for every $n\in\mathbb N$ and every real-valued
function $h$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ with variance at most $1$, the
following holds. If $0<\varepsilon\le1$ and $0<\delta\le1/20$, and every noisy
coordinate influence of $h$ at noise parameter $1-\delta$ is at most $\varepsilon$, then
for every $c\ge0$ and every $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the
difference between the uniform-cube expectation of $\psi(T_{1-\delta}h)$ and its
expectation when the Fourier--Walsh polynomial of $T_{1-\delta}h$ is evaluated on
independent standard Gaussian coordinates has absolute value at most
\[
Kc\,\varepsilon^{\delta/3}.
\]
\end{theorem}

There is a constant $K>0$ such that the following holds. Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let
$(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability spaces, and let $F$ be a multilinear
coefficient family of degree at most $k$ whose Boolean-cube evaluation has variance at
most $1$. For $\varepsilon\ge0$, suppose every coordinate influence is at most
$\varepsilon$. If $X$ and $Y$ are independent coordinate families on the respective
spaces and each coordinate satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions under
its measure, then the Levy distance between the laws of $F(X)$ and $F(Y)$ is at most
\[
K\,2^k\varepsilon^{1/5}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Levy-distance invariance estimate]

\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hypercontractive_radius_le_five_sixths, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_c3_quarter_power_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.levy_bound_of_derivative_map, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_c3, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.levyDistance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp_nat, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_three_halves_influences_le_degree_mul, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.has_degree_at_most_eval, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_nonneg}

There are constants $K,A>0$ such that the following holds. Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let
$(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability spaces, and let $F$ be a multilinear
coefficient family of degree at most $k$ whose Boolean-cube evaluation has variance at
most $1$. For $\varepsilon\ge0$, suppose every coordinate influence of that evaluation
is at most $\varepsilon$. If $X$ and $Y$ are independent coordinate families on the
respective spaces, each coordinate is $(2,3,\rho)$-hypercontractive for some $0<\rho<1$,
and each has mean zero and second moment one, then the Levy distance between the laws of
$F(X)$ and $F(Y)$ is at most
\[
K\left(\frac1\rho\right)^{Ak}\varepsilon^{1/8}.
\]
\end{theorem}
